title: The sheaf localization filtration and its pullback comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $X$ a scheme, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Use ordinary derived categories of constant $A$-module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites and their exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Write $DF^+(X,A)$ for bounded-below complexes with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes, localized at maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every graded quotient; write $\omega$ for forgetting the filtration and $\operatorname{gr}^r$ for the graded quotient. The assignment on complexes
$$F^0S_X(C)=C,\quad F^1S_X(C)=j_!j^*C,\quad F^2S_X(C)=0$$
(with $F^r=C$ for $r<0$ and $F^r=0$ for $r>2$), whose inclusion is the open counit, descends to a functor $S_X:D^+(X,A)\to DF^+(X,A)$, with natural identifications
$$\omega S_X(K)=K,\qquad \operatorname{gr}^1S_X(K)=j_!j^*K,\qquad \operatorname{gr}^0S_X(K)=Ri_*i^*K.$$
Its underlying triangle is the localization triangle with its specified counit and unit.

Let $t:X\to X$, $t_U:U\to U$ and $t_Z:Z\to Z$ satisfy $tj=jt_U$ and $ti=it_Z$, and suppose the open square is Cartesian. The termwise filtered pullback admits a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_t:Lt^*S_X(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_X(Lt^*K).$$
On the total complex it is the identity; on $F^1$ it is the canonical open exchange $b_t:Lt^*j_!j^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!Lt_U^*j^*K$, followed by the pullback-composition identification. On $\operatorname{gr}^0$ it is the ordinary closed-square mate $e_{t,i}:Lt^*Ri_*\to Ri_*Lt_Z^*$ followed by the corresponding pullback identification. This mate is defined by transposition under $Li^*\dashv Ri_*$ and the counit $Li^*Ri_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$; the closed square is not required to be Cartesian.
For any $u:Lt^*K\to K$, the filtered morphism $S_X(u)\circ\alpha_t$ has total map $u$, degree-1 map $j_!(Lj^*u\circ c_j)\circ b_t$, and degree-0 map $Ri_*(Li^*u\circ c_i)\circ e_{t,i}$, where $c_h:Lt_W^*Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lt^*$ is the canonical comparison for $h=j,i$.

proof.text:
Work in constant $A$-module sheaves, without constructibility or completion. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], $j_!$ and $i_*$ are exact, the closed counit $i^*i_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and open unit $\mathrm{id}\simeq j^*j_!$ are invertible, and every sheaf $M$ has the natural exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_!j^*M\xrightarrow{a_M}M\xrightarrow{p_M}i_*i^*M\longrightarrow0,$$
with $a$ the open counit and $p$ the closed unit. The quasi-compactness of $j$ is precisely the complement hypothesis needed for exactness of $i_*$ and for this sequence. All inverse images are exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and compute the ordinary derived functors, in particular $Ri_*=i_*$ on complexes. Exact termwise functors also preserve bounded-below complexes. These sheaf adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and $i^*\dashv i_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] hold for every finite commutative $A$; no $A_{E,n}$ hypothesis is used. On derived categories, [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] gives $j_!\dashv j^*$ with unit and counit the classes of the termwise ones. The derived adjunction $Li^*\dashv Ri_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is the bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]; its characterization with $s,t$ identities, whose cocone maps are the computation isomorphisms above, sends the class of a chain map $f:C\to i_*N$ to that of $\varepsilon_N\,i^*f$. Hence its unit and counit are the classes of the termwise closed unit $p$ and counit $\varepsilon$, under these identifications.

proof.text: For a bounded-below sheaf complex $C$, apply the sequence of Step 1 in every cochain degree. Naturality of $a$ makes its images a subcomplex, canonically identified with $j_!j^*C$. Give $C$ the filtration $F^0=C$, $F^1=j_!j^*C$, $F^2=0$ of the statement. For a chain map $f:C\to D$, take total map $f$ and subcomplex map $j_!j^*f$; the equality $f a_C=a_Dj_!j^*f$ makes this a filtered chain map. Identities and composites are preserved because both component functors preserve them. The graded complexes are naturally $j_!j^*C$ in degree $1$ and $i_*i^*C$ in degree $0$, the latter identified through the quotient map $p_C$. All other graded complexes vanish.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, p. 42: the section on complexes; pro-etale quotient supplied by Tag 09AH

proof.text: If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its two graded maps in Step 2 are quasi-isomorphisms by the exact-functor assertion [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Hence the complex-level section followed by filtered localization inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](1),(2) to obtain $S_X:D^+(X,A)\to DF^+(X,A)$ and its natural graded identifications. Forgetting a finite filtration also descends: in the degreewise short exact sequences $0\to F^{r+1}C\to F^rC\to\operatorname{gr}^rC\to0$, induction downwards from $F^bC=0$ shows that graded quasi-isomorphisms induce quasi-isomorphisms on every $F^rC$, hence on $C$. The induction uses the long exact sequences of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and their comparison diagrams from [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality]: in the five consecutive terms centered at $H^n(F^rC)$ the four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms, so the middle one is an isomorphism. Thus the identity of total complexes gives $\omega S_X\simeq\mathrm{id}$; the quotient and subcomplex identifications give the stated $\operatorname{gr}^0$ and $\operatorname{gr}^1$ functors, with $i_*=Ri_*$ as in Step 1.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, p. 42; homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), functorial cohomology exact sequences

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to $0\to j_!j^*C\xrightarrow{a_C}C\xrightarrow{p_C}i_*i^*C\to0$. It gives the distinguished localization triangle with exactly the displayed open counit and closed unit, including its connecting map; by Step 1 these classes are the derived open counit and the unit of $Li^*\dashv Ri_*$. Its naturality for chain maps, followed by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), gives the same natural triangle on $D^+(X,A)$. This is the underlying subcomplex--total--quotient triangle of the filtration constructed in Step 2.

proof.text:
Exact $t^*$ preserves filtration subobjects, quotients and graded quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], so defines $Lt^*$ on $DF^+$. The Cartesian open square and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] give the natural isomorphism $b_{t,M}:t^*j_!M\simeq j_!t_U^*M$ for every complex $M$ and this finite ring $A$. Put $B_C=j_!(c_{j,C})b_{t,j^*C}$, where $c_j:t_U^*j^*\simeq j^*t^*$ comes from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].
We check its counit normalization. On open slice sites [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] gives $j^*t_*\simeq t_{U*}j^*$; sectionwise this is the Cartesian identification $V\times_XX\simeq V\times_UU$. Thus $t^*j_!$ and $j_!t_U^*$ have canonically identified right adjoints. The composite adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the unique comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] specify the canonical $b_t$. Expanding their unit equation through the two Hom bijections says that $b_{t,M}^{-1}$ is the $j_!\dashv j^*$ transpose of $c_{j,j_!M}\,t_U^*\eta_{j,M}$, with $\eta_j$ the open unit. The slice theorem applies because the base-change site functor for $t$ sends $U$ to $X\times_XU\simeq U$, by the Cartesian hypothesis.
Under $j_!\dashv j^*$, the transpose of $t^*a_C B_C^{-1}$ is the identity: naturality of $c_j$ reduces it to $j^*a_C\eta_{j,j^*C}=1$. The sheaf adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] therefore gives $a_{t^*C}B_C=t^*a_C$. Hence $(1,B_C)$ and $(1,B_C^{-1})$ are inverse filtered chain maps. Their naturality and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) descend them to $\alpha_t$ with the prescribed total and $F^1$ maps.

source.place: Tag 04J0 (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites), with categories.tex Tags 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints) and 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits); open counit normalization; Varshavsky §5.2.2

proof.text:
Identify the quotient comparison directly. Keep $p_C:C\to i_*i^*C$ and write $\varepsilon:i^*i_*\to\mathrm{id}$ for the counit of the sheaf adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $\theta=c_i^{-1}:i^*t^*\simeq t_Z^*i^*$, using [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] the closed mate $e_M:t^*i_*M\to i_*t_Z^*M$ is the transpose of $t_Z^*\varepsilon_M\,\theta_{i_*M}$. Let $m_C=i_*(c_{i,C})e_{i^*C}$. The transpose of $m_Ct^*p_C$ is
$$c_{i,C}\,t_Z^*\varepsilon_{i^*C}\,\theta_{i_*i^*C}\,i^*t^*p_C
=c_{i,C}\,t_Z^*(\varepsilon_{i^*C}i^*p_C)\,\theta_C=1.$$
The first equality is naturality of $\theta$; the second is the closed adjunction triangle identity and $c_i\theta=1$. The transpose of $p_{t^*C}$ is also the identity, so $m_Ct^*p_C=p_{t^*C}$. By Step 1 and exactness of $t^*$, $t^*p_C$ is degreewise epimorphic. Hence $m_C$ is exactly the quotient map induced by $(1,B_C)$ in Step 5, by uniqueness of factorization through a cokernel. By Step 1 the derived mate $e_{t,i}$ is the class of the termwise mate $e$, and on these exact termwise representatives $c_i$ is the class of the termwise comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] (both are natural and agree on K-flat resolutions). Descending this natural equality by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) identifies $\operatorname{gr}^0\alpha_t$ with $Ri_*(c_i)e_{t,i}$. Only $ti=it_Z$ was used; no Cartesian property of the closed square entered the computation.

source.place: §5.2.2, adjunction definition of canonical comparisons; agent calculation for the ordinary pro-etale localization quotient, using the closed unit and counit

proof.text:
For $u:Lt^*K\to K$, functoriality gives $S_X(u)\alpha_t$. Its total map is $u$ because $\omega S_X$ is the identity. The natural identifications of Step 3 give $\operatorname{gr}^1S_X(u)=j_!Lj^*u$ and $\operatorname{gr}^0S_X(u)=Ri_*Li^*u$. Composing these with the maps from Steps 5 and 6 gives, respectively,
$$j_!(Lj^*u\circ c_j)\circ b_t,\qquad Ri_*(Li^*u\circ c_i)\circ e_{t,i}.$$
These identities hold for an arbitrary derived morphism $u$, since all the graded identifications and comparisons are natural transformations on the localized categories, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2),(3); no representative of $u$ as a single chain map is assumed. There is no invertibility condition on $u$.

tool_uses.why: The general constant-module specialization supplies exactness and the specified sheaf counit/unit sequence; the trace unit needs these inputs before constructing its filtered section.
Identifies termwise exact functors with the ordinary bounded-below derived operations, rather than completed operations.
Generic Cartesian open exchange for every finite commutative ring and every sheaf complex, without the special A_E,n restriction of the trace-unit exchange node.
Supplies the canonical restriction comparisons c_j and c_i for scheme maps and the exact coefficient operations.
Generic localized-ringed-site comparison identifies the right adjoints in the Cartesian open square; used only to check the canonical exchange normalization.
Generic uniqueness and unit equation for conjugate left adjoints; makes the canonical open exchange normalization explicit.
Generic identification of the open pro-etale site with the slice site, needed to apply the localized-ringed-site comparison when checking exchange normalization.
